item.title: Art Lounge: Collage Night — Thu Aug 13, 7:00 PM
item.description:
Pull up a chair, pour yourself a drink, and make something beautiful! Art Lounge is your laid-back Thursday night creative escape — no agenda, no pressure, no experience needed. Just good music, great company, and a table full of materials waiting to become something entirely your own. Cut, tear, layer, and arrange your way through the evening at whatever pace feels right. Not sure where to start? We’ve got prompts to spark your imagination and get the ideas flowing. Or ignore them completely and follow your instincts – either way works perfectly here. Bring your friends, bring your BYOB, and leave with a piece of art you actually made. It’s the best kind of Thursday night. 🗓 Thursday, August 13 | 7:00 pm – 8:30 pm 📍 The Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, 2nd Floor, Montclair, NJ 🎟 $10 | All materials provided | BYOB welcome Open to everyone. No art experience needed. Just show up and create.
Source: The Space For Art

item.title: Unearthing Stories of Female Artists in Exile and Resistance — Wed Aug 26, 4:00 PM — Montclair Main - Auditorium
item.description:
Session 2 of a two-part series on Billie Holiday. Join us for a discussion of her landmark 1956 autobiography, marking its 70th anniversary. Written with journalist William Dufty, Lady Sings the Blues is a raw and unflinching account of Holiday's life — her rise as one of jazz's greatest voices, her struggles with racism, addiction, and exploitation, and her refusal to be silenced. Participants receive a copy of the book, available for pickup at the Main Branch. Light refreshments provided. Part of Adult Summer Reading 2026: Unearth a Story.
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306

item.title: Silent Book Club Montclair — Wed Aug 26, 5:00 PM — Montclair - Offsite
item.description:
At Silent Book Club® there's no assigned reading. SBC members gather in bars, cafés, bookstores, libraries, and online to read together in quiet camaraderie. All readers are welcome—ebooks or audiobooks, poetry or prose, fiction or non-fiction... it's BYOBook.
Did you love silent reading time in school? Are you more of an introvert that loves books, but doesn't want to jump into a discussion group? Are you looking to read more, but struggle to sit down and just DO IT? If you answered 'yes' to any of these, you might like Silent Book Club! Each month, we meet around Montclair and enjoy each other's company with a book of our own choosing.
Registration is required. We will be meeting at Porter Park in Montclair for all summer meetings! In the event of rain, an alternate location will be chosen.
Please be advised this book club will be meeting at a public location and therefore cannot guarantee a quiet reading environment. This book club is best for readers who enjoy a coffeeshop ambi

item.title: Tech Talks: What To Do When Something Goes Wrong — Thu Aug 27, 3:30 PM — Montclair Main - Classroom
item.description:
Tech Talks is a free informational series where library staff introduce and explain the technology topics that matter most in today's digital world. Each session takes a closer look at a new or complex topic—whether it's a trending app, an emerging technology, or a platform you've been hearing about but aren't quite sure how to navigate. Through demonstrations and clear, jargon-free explanations, you'll come away with a better understanding of the tech landscape around you. There's no hands-on component, so no devices are needed—just come ready to learn and ask questions.
All are welcome regardless of experience level, and time is reserved at the end of each session for Q&A. Sessions are free and open to the public.
This week's topic is: What To Do When Something Goes Wrong

item.description:
This month we will be reading "Fruit Fly" by Josh Silver.
A BBC must-read book of 2026—”Sharp, dark and humorous, it’s a real nail-biter.”
Go gay. Go sad. Go dark.
A washed-up author will stop at nothing to claw her way back to relevancy—even if it means appropriating a young gay man’s tragic story.
Mallory Maddox is buried under seven years of writer’s block. With her status as a literary sensation fizzling, she’ll do anything she can to resurrect her career. Inspiration needs to strike—and fast.
Enter Leo. He’s a struggling addict sleeping under bridges and trading sex for survival. He’s vulnerable. He’s enigmatic. He’s exactly what Mallory has been looking for.
Mallory needs Leo if she wants another bestseller. The world needs Leo’s story right now, and Mallory believes she deserves to tell it. Really, it’s her story—she’s the one who wrote it, after all.

item.description: UNRECYCLABLE: Look Again – Assemblage Art by Andrew Borg Opening Reception: Friday, August 14, 5 – 8pm The Space presents Unrecyclable: Look Again, a solo exhibition of assemblage art by Andrew Borg composed predominantly of the unrecyclable plastics, foams, and composites he refused to throw away for nearly two years — the molded trays, caps, and packaging inserts that carry no recycling code and vanish into the trash without a thought. The exhibition, culminating Borg’s year as Artist in Residence at The Space, is on view August 14–22, 2026, with an opening reception Friday, August 14, from 5 to 8pm. What began as an act of defiance gradually became an act of appreciation: these are highly engineered, purpose-built objects, molded to cushion, position, and protect — aesthetic objects in their own right, designed by someone, meant to be forgotten by everyone. item.description: Assemblage Lab & Gallery Talk with Andrew Borg Closing Event for “Unrecyclable: Look Again” What do you see when you really look at what you throw away? Join artist Andrew Borg for the closing event of Unrecyclable: Look Again — an afternoon that begins with a gallery talk and ends with your hands deep in materials you never thought twice about discarding. After walking through the exhibition and sharing the story behind his two-year collection of unrecyclable plastics, foams, and composites, Borg leads an immersive hands-on Assemblage Lab in which participants get to experience the process firsthand. Using unrecyclable packaging, abandoned electronics, appliances, and other “ghost objects,” you’ll build your own assemblage, sculpture, or mixed-media artwork — guided by the same impulse that drove this exhibition: look again. Prepare to launch into the darkest depths of deep space! Join us as we sit down with master storyteller Daniel Kraus, winner of the 2026 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction, to celebrate the release of his breathtaking new novel, The Sixth Nik.
Deep into space, far past the triworld outposts, beyond range of the lethal trollbot internet, soars The Sickness: a ship woven from biomatter and capable of reacting to every need of its human crew. Sisilla, a nine-year-old cultist with a brain enhanced by arcane tech known as “niks,” has boarded to investigate the enigma of Fém—a plague-riddled planet that has abruptly gone rogue.
The mysterious crew includes a faceless assassin, a beautiful engineer jigsawed by plastic surgery, a peyote-addicted medic, and—most lethal of all—a rugged, NonModded captain with a score to settle with Sisilla. Other dangers abound. A hacked robot begins to believe Sisilla is its daughter.
